issues.description: meta field conflates opaque metadata with renderer configuration in one untyped channel
issues.detail: Docs explicitly use meta for both contextual metadata (versions, timestamps) and renderer hints (Mermaid layout, code language, textStyle CSS). This complects two unrelated contracts through one dict and leaks renderer concerns into the abstraction. Separate render_config from meta, or document reserved keys and per-renderer schemas explicitly.

issues.description: Closure 'data context' example contradicts its framing by capturing a literal at construction time
issues.detail: The make_preview_fn example closes over a hardcoded sample_data list defined at pipeline-construction time and calls it 'data context.' The preview looks live but is frozen. Either show actually loading from the catalog inside preview_fn, or drop the section and state plainly when the snapshot is taken.

issues.description: preview_fn signature, error semantics, and input/output access limitation are unspecified
issues.detail: Docs admit preview_fn has no access to node inputs/outputs but treat closures as the pattern rather than naming the limitation. The required signature (zero-arg? async?), exception propagation, and what node.preview() returns when preview_fn is absent are never stated. Pin the contract and surface the limitation explicitly.

issues.description: Preview supertype contract is absent; behavior documented by example only
issues.detail: The family of Preview subtypes is introduced without stating the abstract contract: required fields, per-subtype content preconditions (TablePreview requires list[dict] while peers accept natural types), to_dict() guarantees, or invariants. Without a written ADT spec, LSP substitution and future subtypes are fragile.

issues.description: CustomPreview renderer_key contract leaks Kedro-Viz coupling without specifying ownership
issues.detail: CustomPreview's renderer_key identifies a frontend component but the docs never specify who owns the namespace, what happens on unknown keys, or how the kedro/kedro-viz boundary is contracted. This leaks a frontend dependency through the node API. Define ownership and failure modes before leaving experimental.

issues.description: Seven Preview subclasses where a tagged value would suffice
issues.detail: JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, and CustomPreview differ only by a renderer tag and content shape — a discriminated union wearing a class hierarchy. CustomPreview with renderer_key already proves the general case. Worth flagging upstream; docs should at least note the pattern.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this docs-only PR is competent at the surface but normalizes several complected design choices it should instead name. The dominant concern across all three reviewers is the overloaded meta field, which mixes opaque metadata with renderer configuration in one untyped channel. Hickey and Pike both call out the closure 'data context' example for contradicting its own framing by capturing a literal at pipeline-construction time, and Hickey and Liskov both flag that preview_fn's signature, error semantics, and input/output access limitation are unspecified. Liskov adds that the Preview supertype lacks a written contract and that CustomPreview's renderer_key leaks Kedro-Viz coupling. The seven-subclass hierarchy reads as a discriminated union to multiple reviewers and is worth flagging upstream.
